svg.title: The two lambda formulas saturate at opposite ends
svg.desc: A plot of the regularisation strength lambda against the largest eigenvalue of the scatter matrix on a log scale. Equation 3's exponential curve falls to zero almost immediately, while Algorithm 1's sigmoid rises to one just as fast. A shaded band marks the range of eigenvalues measured on realistically sized scatter matrices, which lies far to the right of both transitions, so within that band one formula returns zero and the other returns one.
svg.text: σ, the largest eigenvalue of the scatter matrix (log scale)
The paper gives two different λ, and at a = 4 they saturate at opposite ends
Equation 3 shrinks λ to 0, leaving S̃_W = S_W — still singular when features
outnumber samples per class. Algorithm 1 drives λ to 1, making S̃_W = I, so within-class
scatter leaves Reg-FDA entirely. Neither is the intermediate shrinkage described.
